topics.label: Unit Testing
topics.desc: Isolated verification of the smallest testable units (functions, classes) in fast, deterministic feedback loops that anchor any test suite.

topics.label: Integration Testing
topics.desc: Verifies that collaborating modules, services, or a unit and its real dependencies (DB, queue) interoperate correctly across their boundaries.

topics.label: End-to-End Testing
topics.desc: Exercises a full user workflow through the deployed system to confirm all layers behave together as the user experiences them.

topics.label: Component Testing
topics.desc: Tests a single deployable service or UI component in isolation with its dependencies stubbed, sitting between unit and integration scope.

topics.label: Test Pyramid
topics.desc: Heuristic favoring many fast unit tests, fewer integration tests, and minimal slow E2E tests to balance coverage against speed and cost.

topics.label: Smoke & Sanity Tests
topics.desc: Shallow, broad checks of critical paths run after a build or deploy to confirm the system is stable enough for deeper testing.

topics.label: Acceptance Testing
topics.desc: Validates that delivered behavior satisfies business requirements and acceptance criteria, often the gate for sign-off or release.

topics.label: Equivalence Partitioning
topics.desc: Divides inputs into classes that should behave identically so one representative per class covers the whole partition efficiently.

topics.label: Boundary Value Analysis
topics.desc: Targets edges of input ranges (min, max, off-by-one) where defects cluster most densely, complementing equivalence classes.

topics.label: Decision Tables
topics.desc: Systematically enumerates combinations of conditions and resulting actions to derive cases for complex business rules.

topics.label: Code Coverage Metrics
topics.desc: Quantifies which lines, branches, or paths tests exercise; useful for finding gaps but a poor direct proxy for test quality.

topics.label: Property-Based Testing
topics.desc: Generates many randomized inputs to check invariants hold, with shrinking to minimal failing cases, surfacing edge bugs example tests miss.

topics.label: Error Guessing
topics.desc: Experience-driven design that anticipates likely fault modes (nulls, empties, overflows) to craft targeted cases beyond formal techniques.

topics.label: Mutation Testing
topics.desc: Seeds small code mutants and checks whether tests catch them, measuring real fault-detection strength instead of mere coverage.

topics.label: Combinatorial Testing
topics.desc: Uses pairwise or n-wise selection to cover interactions among many parameters with far fewer cases than exhaustive combinations.

topics.label: Red-Green-Refactor
topics.desc: The TDD loop: write a failing test, make it pass minimally, then refactor under green, driving design through incremental verification.

topics.label: Test-Driven Development
topics.desc: Discipline of writing tests before code to specify behavior, shape APIs, and keep regression safety nets continuously in place.

topics.label: Behavior-Driven Development
topics.desc: Frames tests as shared, business-readable behavior specifications to align developers, QA, and stakeholders on intended outcomes.

topics.label: Gherkin & Given-When-Then
topics.desc: Structured natural-language syntax for BDD scenarios that maps directly to executable step definitions (e.g., Cucumber).

topics.label: Specification by Example
topics.desc: Captures requirements as concrete, executable examples that double as living documentation and acceptance criteria.

topics.label: Outside-In TDD
topics.desc: London-school approach starting from acceptance tests and driving inward with mocks, contrasting with classicist state-based TDD.

topics.label: Acceptance Test-Driven Dev
topics.desc: Collaborative practice of agreeing on acceptance tests before implementation so the team builds to a shared definition of done.

topics.label: Test Doubles Taxonomy
topics.desc: Meszaros's classification of dummies, stubs, spies, mocks, and fakes by how each stands in for a real collaborator.

topics.label: Mocks
topics.desc: Preprogrammed doubles that assert expected interactions occurred, enabling behavior verification of how code calls collaborators.

topics.label: Stubs
topics.desc: Doubles returning canned responses to feed the unit under test specific inputs without invoking real dependencies.

topics.label: Fakes
topics.desc: Lightweight working implementations (e.g., in-memory DB) that behave realistically but are unsuited for production.

topics.label: Spies
topics.desc: Doubles that record how they were called for later assertions, blending real or stubbed behavior with interaction capture.

topics.label: Dependency Injection for Tests
topics.desc: Supplying collaborators externally so tests can substitute doubles, the seam that makes isolation and unit testing tractable.

topics.label: Test Isolation
topics.desc: Ensuring each test runs independently with no shared mutable state or ordering dependence, preventing flaky cross-contamination.

topics.label: Over-Mocking Pitfalls
topics.desc: Risk that excessive mocking couples tests to implementation detail, yielding brittle suites that pass while the system breaks.

topics.label: Test Frameworks & Runners
topics.desc: Tooling (JUnit, pytest, Jest) providing assertions, fixtures, discovery, and reporting that structures and executes automated tests.

topics.label: CI Test Integration
topics.desc: Running suites automatically on every commit or PR to gate merges, the backbone of continuous integration feedback.

topics.label: Flaky Test Management
topics.desc: Detecting, quarantining, and root-causing nondeterministic tests that erode trust in the suite and stall pipelines.

topics.label: Test Data Management
topics.desc: Provisioning, factories, fixtures, and cleanup strategies that give tests realistic, isolated, repeatable data states.

topics.label: UI Test Automation
topics.desc: Driving browsers or apps via Selenium, Playwright, or Cypress to automate end-to-end user-facing scenarios reliably.

topics.label: Visual Regression Testing
topics.desc: Captures and diffs rendered screenshots to catch unintended UI changes that functional assertions overlook.

topics.label: Contract Testing
topics.desc: Verifies provider and consumer agree on an API schema (e.g., Pact) so services evolve independently without breaking integrations.

topics.label: Snapshot Testing
topics.desc: Records serialized output and flags changes on rerun, fast to write but prone to rubber-stamped, low-signal updates.

topics.label: Linting
topics.desc: Automated stylistic and correctness checks (ESLint, Pylint) catching bug patterns and enforcing conventions before runtime.

topics.label: Static Type Checking
topics.desc: Compile-time verification of type usage (mypy, TypeScript) that eliminates broad classes of errors without executing code.

topics.label: Data-Flow Analysis
topics.desc: Tracks how values propagate through code to detect uninitialized reads, dead stores, taint, and resource-leak defects.

topics.label: SAST Security Scanning
topics.desc: Static application security testing that inspects source for vulnerable patterns like injection sinks and hardcoded secrets.

topics.label: Code Formatters
topics.desc: Deterministic auto-formatters (Prettier, Black, gofmt) that remove style debate and keep diffs focused on substance.

topics.label: Complexity Metrics
topics.desc: Quantifies maintainability via cyclomatic complexity, coupling, and cognitive load to flag refactor-worthy hotspots.

topics.label: Rule Config & False Positives
topics.desc: Tuning rule sets, baselines, and suppressions so analyzers stay actionable rather than drowning teams in noise.

topics.label: Load Testing
topics.desc: Simulates expected concurrent demand to confirm a system meets throughput and latency targets under realistic traffic.

topics.label: Stress Testing
topics.desc: Pushes load beyond capacity to find the breaking point and observe failure and recovery behavior at the limits.

topics.label: Soak Testing
topics.desc: Sustains moderate load for hours or days to surface slow degradations like memory leaks and resource exhaustion.

topics.label: Spike Testing
topics.desc: Applies sudden sharp traffic surges to verify elastic scaling and graceful handling of abrupt demand changes.

topics.label: Latency & Throughput Metrics
topics.desc: Measuring percentile latency, throughput, and error rates against SLOs to define and judge acceptable performance.

topics.label: Load Testing Tools
topics.desc: Generators like JMeter, k6, Gatling, and Locust that script virtual users and aggregate performance results at scale.

topics.label: Benchmarking & Microbenchmarks
topics.desc: Controlled measurement of code or component performance, guarding against warmup, noise, and measurement bias.

topics.label: Formal Specification
topics.desc: Precise mathematical description of intended system behavior (e.g., TLA+, Z) enabling rigorous reasoning before or instead of code.

topics.label: Model Checking
topics.desc: Exhaustively explores a system's state space against temporal-logic properties to find deadlocks and safety violations.

topics.label: Theorem Proving
topics.desc: Machine-checked deductive proofs (Coq, Isabelle, Lean) establishing correctness with mathematical certainty for critical code.

topics.label: Design by Contract
topics.desc: Specifying preconditions, postconditions, and invariants as enforceable obligations between callers and components.

topics.label: Invariants & Assertions
topics.desc: Embedding checkable correctness conditions in code to fail fast on violated assumptions, a pragmatic bridge to formal rigor.

topics.label: Symbolic Execution
topics.desc: Runs programs on symbolic inputs to systematically explore paths and auto-generate inputs reaching deep or buggy states.

topics.label: SMT & Constraint Solvers
topics.desc: Decision procedures (Z3) over logical theories that underpin model checking, symbolic execution, and verification tooling.
